formationLabel: Lithuanian Catholic mission care documented from 1917 · parish organized about 1919 · territorial by 1926 · closed December 30, 1989
currentUse: The former St. Peter church at 795 Russell Avenue was demolished after the parish closed. The Diocese of Cleveland's current directory places its Social Action Office at 795 Russell Avenue, documenting Catholic institutional use of the site but not survival of the parish or former church structure. St. Peter's sacramental records are now held by the Diocesan Archives.
summary: St. Peter was Akron's Lithuanian Roman Catholic parish. Lithuanian mission care is documented from 1917, the parish was organized about 1919, and it became a territorial parish open beyond the Lithuanian community by 1926. It continued at 795 Russell Avenue until closing on December 30, 1989; the Diocese of Cleveland's records directory gives a 1917-1989 sacramental-record span and current archival custody. The former church was demolished, while the Russell Avenue site now houses diocesan social-action offices.

historicalNarrative.text: Akron's St. Peter began as ministry for Lithuanian Catholics. Wolkovich's Volume 3 history places mission care in 1917 and parish organization under Father Janusas about 1919. These are distinct milestones: 1917 marks the documented mission and sacramental-record phase, while about 1919 is the attributed parish-organization date. The exact canonical erection instrument remains unresolved.

historicalNarrative.text: By 1926 St. Peter had become a territorial parish open to Catholics beyond its Lithuanian founders. That pastoral and ethnic-status transition did not close or replace the parish; it describes the same Roman Catholic institution serving a broader local population. No decree for the transition has been located.

sources.locator: Wolkovich, Lithuanian Religious Life in America, Vol. 3, printed pp. 45-46

historicalNarrative.text: The parish's later church was at 795 Russell Avenue. A 1984 Akron Reporter item identifies St. Peter Catholic Church at that address and describes its Saturday meal service, proving active parish and site use near the end of the institution's life. The available sources do not establish the church's construction or dedication date or every earlier worship location.

historicalNarrative.text: Wolkovich's Volume 3 history dates St. Peter's closure to December 30, 1989 and describes it as Akron's first Catholic church to close. The Diocese of Cleveland's current table independently places St. Peter among closed and merged institutions and gives its records as 1917-1989. Because that official table labels the dates as a record span, it corroborates the closed context and terminal year but does not by itself prove the exact closing day or canonical mechanism.

historicalNarrative.text: The former St. Peter church was later demolished, while 795 Russell Avenue remained in Catholic institutional use. The Diocese of Cleveland's 2025 directory lists its Social Action Office at that address. This is site reuse after parish closure, not evidence that the church building survived or that St. Peter continued under another name; the Diocesan Archives separately hold the sacramental records.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: The official diocesan table labels 1917-1989 as dates of records, not explicit canonical erection and suppression dates. Wolkovich's Volume 3 history distinguishes 1917 mission care from parish organization about 1919 and supplies December 30, 1989 as the exact closure reading. The former Lithuanian national parish's territorial transition by 1926 was a pastoral-status change, not closure or replacement.
gaps: The exact host church during the mission phase; the canonical erection instrument and precise formation date; the Russell Avenue church's construction, dedication, and demolition dates; the closure decree and final-Mass documentation; the relationship of highway acquisition to the terminal event; complete records coverage; any cemetery; and the precise footprint of current buildings on the former church parcel remain unresolved.
